title: Mukesh Ambani Just Told Shareholders That Jio Studios Owned 40% of India's Box Office. He Wasn't Exaggerating.
excerpt: In his annual letter, the Reliance chairman highlighted the Dhurandhar franchise's back-to-back record runs and Jyoti Deshpande's transformation of the studio into Bollywood's undisputed market leader.
body:
When Mukesh Ambani decides to talk about movies in his annual letter to Reliance shareholders, it usually means the numbers are too big to ignore. This year, the numbers are historic.

In his FY 2025-26 shareholder letter, Ambani singled out Jio Studios and its flagship Dhurandhar franchise as the crown jewel of Reliance's entertainment portfolio. "It achieved an unprecedented 40%+ of India's box office," he wrote, a figure that would have been unthinkable for any single studio even five years ago.

The Dhurandhar franchise — a pair of geopolitical spy thrillers directed by Aditya Dhar — has rewritten the rules of Indian film distribution. The first installment arrived in theatres in December 2025 and became a cultural phenomenon. Its sequel, Dhurandhar: The Revenge, followed just three months later in March 2026, an aggressive release strategy that Ambani himself acknowledged was unprecedented.

"Never before in the world, let alone India, had a film franchise been conceived, financed and shot as two parts and released so close to each other," Ambani stated in the letter.

## Three Years at the Top

But the Dhurandhar franchise is not a one-off. Ambani pointed to a streak that has no parallel in Bollywood history: "Jio Studios has achieved the unique distinction of having the highest-grossing film three years in a row with Stree 2 in 2024, Dhurandhar in 2025 and Dhurandhar The Revenge in 2026, demonstrating consistency and undisputed leadership."

That consistency is what separates Jio Studios from the traditional studio model in India. Legacy banners like Yash Raj Films and Dharma Productions built their empires on star-driven franchises and genre templates — spy thrillers for YRF, romantic dramas for Dharma. Jio Studios, under the leadership of Jyoti Deshpande, has taken a different approach: backing diverse subjects across budgets, from Kiran Rao's Laapataa Ladies (India's Oscar entry in 2025) to the horror-comedy Stree 2, to the high-octane Dhurandhar series.

## What This Means for Diaspora Audiences

For NRI moviegoers in the US, UK, and Canada, the Dhurandhar franchise has been a rare unifying cultural moment. Both films opened to packed houses in overseas markets, with the franchise crossing ₹500 crore internationally — numbers that put it in the same conversation as global tentpole releases.

The franchise's appeal to diaspora audiences is not accidental. Its themes of national security, intelligence operations, and India's place on the global stage resonate with viewers who navigate multiple national identities daily. The films offered something Bollywood rarely delivers: a big-budget Indian narrative that felt genuinely global in its ambitions.

## The Deshpande Factor

Industry analysts credit much of the studio's transformation to Jyoti Deshpande, who heads Jio Studios' operations. Trade analyst Atul Mohan noted that unlike other banners, Jio Studios does not rely on a single franchise template. "They are trying multiple things and they are being successful also. It is very commendable that a new studio has achieved this."

Deshpande's strategy has been to greenlight scripts based on story strength rather than star power, a philosophy that allowed the studio to back unconventional projects that larger banners might have passed on. The result is a slate that includes horror comedies, political dramas, indie darlings, and now a franchise that Ambani himself calls a benchmark in "box office, release strategy, monetisation models and customer engagement."

## The Bigger Picture

Ambani's shareholder letter is ultimately a document about returns on investment, and the entertainment division is delivering them. But for Indian cinema, the subtext is more significant: the era of the director-producer-star nexus is giving way to a studio-led model where institutional capital, strategic distribution, and franchise thinking drive the business.

Jio Studios is not the only player making this shift — Disney Star, Amazon, and Netflix are all investing heavily in Indian content. But as of this moment, no other studio can claim what Ambani put in writing this week: three consecutive years with the biggest film in India.

Whether that dominance holds will depend on what comes next. For now, the numbers speak clearly enough.
